questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector To a Plane Given by Parametric Equation
questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 12 \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨3,0,4⟩$ and $w=⟨1,-1,1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =4i+j-3k \\  & =⟨4,1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨4,1,-3⟩.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨4,1,-3⟩.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Lines
questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $D(6,2,1)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨\frac{1}{2},1,9⟩+s⟨4,-1,5⟩$ and $r=⟨\sqrt{3},10,-1⟩+t⟨0,2,3⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨4,-1,5⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,2,3⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $D(6,2,1)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $d=⟨6,2,1⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =d+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨6,2,1⟩+s⟨4,-1,5⟩+t⟨0,2,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Passing Through Three Given Points
questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $C(1,1,1)$ and $D(-3,2,4)$, and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨0,1,1⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). We already have one vector $v=⟨0,1,1⟩.$ Let's also use the displacement vector $\overset{\to }{CD}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CD} & =⟨-3,2,4⟩-⟨1,1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,1,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $c=⟨1,1,1⟩$ of the point $C,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+sv+t\overset{\to }{CD} \\ r & =⟨1,1,1⟩+s⟨0,1,1⟩+t⟨-4,1,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Lines
questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $E(4,-2,5)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨11,0,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and $r=⟨12,-2,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨3,-5,1⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $E(4,-2,5)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $e=⟨4,-2,5⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =e+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨4,-2,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Passing Through Three Given Points
questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $U(7,-2,3),\,V(4,4,-4),$ and $W(3,7,6).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{UV}$ and $\overset{\to }{UW},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{UV} & =⟨4,4,-4⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,6,-7⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{UW} & =⟨3,7,6⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,9,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $u=⟨7,-2,3⟩$ of the point $U,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =u+s\overset{\to }{UV}+t\overset{\to }{UW} \\ r & =⟨7,-2,3⟩+s⟨-3,6,-7⟩+t⟨-4,9,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Passing Through Three Given Points
